overrideReason: All 3 automated attempts failed with '0/6 - not judged, a cheaper layer already failed'. This was NOT the temp-directory environment class of failure - it was a genuine, unanticipated architectural gap this project's own board model had never needed to solve before: FRED's seven macro series are market-wide, not per-asset, but web/src/board.ts's BOARD_ASSETS was hardcoded to ["BTC","ETH","SOL","BNB"], and buildBoard's familyOf() strictly requires every registry key to start with one of those four asset prefixes. The implementer registered the seven entries with definable_for: [MACRO] (correctly anticipating a pseudo-asset bucket) but used vendor-prefixed keys (fred_vixcls, etc.) instead of asset-prefixed ones, and never extended BOARD_ASSETS - so buildBoard threw 'Registry key fred_vixcls does not begin with its asset prefix macro_' and the entire web suite failed before any criterion could be judged. This required a real product decision the automated pipeline could not make on its own: the owner was asked directly (via AskUserQuestion) whether market-wide data should appear as a 5th pseudo-asset column alongside BTC/ETH/SOL/BNB, or as a separate section outside the per-asset grid. The owner chose the 5th-column approach. Implemented directly: (1) web/src/board.ts's BOARD_ASSETS now includes "MACRO" as a 5th value, with a comment documenting the decision and its date; (2) renamed all seven registry keys from fred_* to macro_* to match the asset-prefix convention every other entry uses, across ingest/registry.yaml, tests/test_registry.py, and web/src/board.test.ts; (3) removed one test the implementer had added (web/src/board.test.ts's 'registry entries for assets outside this board are left for their own panel') whose own premise - that MACRO-tagged entries should be silently excluded from the board - directly contradicted the owner's chosen design, once confirmed via git diff that this test was net-new to this story's own attempt, not pre-existing; (4) updated the resulting hardcoded board-cell-count assertions across web/src/board.test.ts, web/src/BoardMatrix.test.tsx, and web/src/CoverageHeadline.test.tsx to the new real totals (27 families, 5 assets, 135 total cells in the mixed fixture) - the same 'hardcoded count tax' every prior story adding a family has hit, now compounded by adding a full column rather than one row. ingest/registry.py required no change; definable_for was already validated as a free-form non-empty string tuple, not a fixed BTC/ETH/SOL/BNB enum. Note for a future story: US-806 (Fear & Greed) is also market-wide and will need the same macro_* key convention and MACRO asset, now already available.

results.note: All seven confirmed series (macro_vixcls, macro_dff, macro_t10y2y, macro_dfii10, macro_dtwexbgs, macro_cpiaucsl, macro_m2sl) are registered, each with response_model: fred_series_observations using US-802's shared fetcher. No more, no fewer - confirmed by direct registry read.

macro_dtwexbgs: expected_update_interval_seconds=604800 (7 days, weekly H.10 cadence), freshness_warn_seconds=864000 (10 days) - sized against the real weekly release, not a daily assumption. Confirmed by direct registry read.

macro_cpiaucsl and macro_m2sl: expected_update_interval_seconds=2678400 (31 days, monthly), freshness_warn_seconds=3888000 (45 days) - sized against their real monthly release cadences. Confirmed by direct registry read.

Every new entry's uncorroborated.note reads 'FRED mirrors the Fed/BLS directly; a second source would check the mirror against its origin rather than provide genuine independent corroboration' - the G1-confirmed decision disclosed on the registry entry itself. Confirmed by direct registry read.
assert_registry_coverage passes for all seven new entries - confirmed via the full offline suite passing (304 passed, includes registry coverage tests).

`uv run pytest -q -m "not integration"` re-run fresh against current HEAD (after the BOARD_ASSETS fix and hardcoded-count updates): 304 passed, 53 deselected, exit 0. `npm --prefix web run typecheck` and `npm --prefix web test` (52 passed) both clean. `uv run mypy ingest --strict` and `uv run ruff check` both clean.

note: All 6 criteria independently verified against current HEAD. This story's real blocker was a genuine architecture gap (no representation for market-wide, non-per-asset data in the board model) that neither the brief, spec, nor stories anticipated when written - resolved via an explicit owner decision (5th pseudo-asset column) rather than a quiet override, since it is product-visible and affects how the whole board reads. The fix is now available for US-806 (Fear & Greed), which has the identical market-wide-data problem.
